question.problem:
Given that the function

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2x+1}, & x<4 \\ ax, & x\ge 4\end{aligned}
$$

is continuous at $x=4,$ find the value of the constant $a.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=4,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\sqrt{2x+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2(4)+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}g(x) & =g(4)=4a.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=4,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}g(x) \\ 3 & =4a \\ a & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
